summary_rationale: Laurus Labs has executed a credible structural pivot from an ARV-heavy generic supplier toward an innovator-led CDMO platform: CDMO reached 41.9% of H1 FY27 revenue (up 71% YoY), gross margins expanded above 60%, H1 FY27 EBITDA margin hit 33.2%, USFDA compliance remained clean across Hyderabad (zero 483s) and Vizag Unit-4 (EIR), and FY26 CFO surged to Rs 1,624 Cr (182% of PAT) with Rs 560 Cr FCF. However, the business remains CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL rather than an unconditional compounder due to high capital intensity (cumulative FY16-FY25 FCF of only Rs 329 Cr; CWIP rising again to Rs 1,282 Cr in Sep 2026 with Rs 3,000+ Cr FY27-28 capex planned), 317 inventory days in FY26 (263-day cash conversion cycle), Rs 2,625 Cr of gross borrowings, a potential interest capitalization forensic flag, and historical earnings cyclicality (FY24 PAT collapsed 80% post-Paxlovid with 3-year ROE at 10.4%). KPI health is PASS_WITH_WATCH: CDMO mix, pipeline depth (125+ projects), and >60% gross margins pass strongly, while inventory normalization and capex-to-ROCE conversion require ongoing monitoring.
